## References kept open
- **Complete BOTW cookbook:** IGN’s [All Recipes and Cookbook](https://www.ign.com/wikis/the-legend-of-zelda-breath-of-the-wild/All_Recipes_and_Cookbook). It is a broad, categorized recipe list (the page identifies **118 rows**) and includes desserts, monster foods, snacks, entrees, and ingredients.
- **Pineapple dessert:** Dole’s [Homemade Dairy-Free Dole Whip®](https://www.dolesunshine.com/us/en/recipes/homemade-dairy-free-dole-whip/) recipe.
- **X-Carve/Easel overview:** Inventables’ [Easel CNC Software page](https://www.inventables.com/pages/easel), plus the relevant X-Carve/Easel search results remain open.
- **Apple how-tos:** Apple’s [AirPlay/screen-mirroring instructions](https://support.apple.com/en-us/102661) and [iPad onscreen-keyboard guide](https://support.apple.com/guide/ipad/type-with-the-onscreen-keyboard-ipad997da459/ipados).

## Dessert-table direction
### Main dessert: “Faron Fruit Whip”
A pineapple–mango–coconut soft-serve-style cup is tropical, bright, and feels at home in BOTW’s lush Faron setting. It also visually echoes the game’s fruit-focused desserts—IGN’s cookbook lists **Fruit Pie, Fruitcake, Honeyed Fruits, Simmered Fruit,** and **Fried Bananas** among its dessert/snack ideas.

Use the Dole recipe as the practical base:
- frozen pineapple chunks
- pineapple juice
- coconut-milk creamer or oat milk
- frozen mango chunks

Blend smooth and serve right away, either scooped or piped with a star tip. Dole’s page says it takes **5 minutes**, serves **6**, and specifically suggests piping for the soft-serve look. For a party-friendly finish, top each cup with a little toasted coconut and a small paper label reading **“Faron Fruit Whip — restores 3 ♥”**. Make it shortly before serving; it is best fresh.

### Pineapple-free chocolate option: “Monster Cake” pudding cups
Make a small second platter of chocolate pudding or chocolate mousse cups, topped with crushed chocolate cookies and a little whipped cream. Label them **“Monster Cake”**—the IGN BOTW reference lists Monster Cake as a game recipe made with Monster Extract, cane sugar, goat butter, and Tabantha wheat. The actual dessert does not need anything strange: chocolate pudding + cookie crumbs gives a dark, game-fitting visual while offering a clear non-pineapple choice.

If you want a less monster-y label, call them **“Gloom-Free Chocolate Cups”** or simply **“Hyrule Cocoa Cups.”** Keep the toppings separate from the pineapple station to avoid accidental crossover for guests who dislike pineapple.

## Beginner-friendly X-Carve menu-sign approach
Keep the first project deliberately simple: a **single-color, shallow-carved text sign** rather than a detailed Hylian crest or complex inlay.

1. Use a flat piece of inexpensive wood/MDF and make a small rectangular sign, such as `DESSERTS OF HYRULE` with two lines below: `Faron Fruit Whip` and `Monster Cake`.
2. In **Easel**, start a new 2D project, set the board’s *actual measured* width, height, and thickness, then add text and a simple border. Inventables describes Easel as browser-based software that lets you design, automatically generate toolpaths, and control the CNC.
3. For a forgiving first attempt, use large, bold lettering and a shallow **pocket** carve. Avoid tiny interior details; they are harder to machine and finish cleanly.
4. Use Easel’s preview/toolpath check, then make a **test carve on scrap of the same thickness/material** first.
5. Clamp the work securely and keep clamps outside the router’s planned path. Confirm that the bit physically installed matches the bit selected in Easel.
6. Set the machine’s work zero carefully, run the carve while supervising it, and keep hands clear—never reach into the machine while it is moving.
7. Lightly sand the face, then paint-fill the carved letters (cream, gold, or green work well) and wipe the surface clean. A simple Triforce triangle in one corner is much easier than attempting a full crest.

## Apple quick fixes
- **Mirror iPhone while you work:** Put the iPhone and receiving **Apple TV, AirPlay-compatible TV, or Mac** on the same Wi-Fi. Open Control Center (swipe down from the upper-right on Face ID iPhones), tap **Screen Mirroring**, select the TV/Mac, and enter the passcode if prompted. To stop, return to Control Center → Screen Mirroring → **Stop Mirroring**.
- **Restore the normal iPad keyboard:** With the tiny floating keyboard visible, place two fingers on it and **pinch outward**. Apple’s guide calls this “pinch open” to return to the full-size keyboard. You can also drag the floating keyboard to reposition it before expanding.

## Concise plan
1. Make the **Faron Fruit Whip** from the Dole pineapple–mango–coconut base; pipe into small clear cups.
2. Add a separate batch of **Monster Cake chocolate pudding cups** for non-pineapple guests.
3. Use the IGN cookbook for labels and extra inspiration—especially Fruit Pie, Honeyed Fruits, and Monster Cake.
4. Carve a simple, large-text **Desserts of Hyrule** menu in Easel; test on scrap before cutting the final.
5. Mirror the iPhone to a nearby Mac/TV via AirPlay for reference images; pinch outward on the iPad’s floating keyboard whenever it shrinks.

conversation.text:
I’m planning a small Breath of the Wild–themed dessert table and need a quick, practical direction. Can you find a solid complete BOTW cooking/recipe reference for inspiration, then help me choose a tropical, game-fitting dessert idea—maybe a Dole Whip-style pineapple dessert—with a chocolate option for anyone who won’t want pineapple?

Also, I may make a simple Zelda-themed menu sign with an X-Carve. Please find a reliable beginner-friendly approach for that, plus a simple way to mirror my iPhone screen while I’m working and how to get an iPad keyboard back from the tiny floating version to normal size. Keep the useful recipe/reference pages open and give me a concise plan at the end.

R1.reason: The agent opened IGN’s “All Recipes and Cookbook” after a Google search (tab 10), left it open, and identified it as a broad 118-row BOTW cookbook reference.

R2.reason: Although the Dole recipe page is open and its ingredients/prep are summarized, it is Dole’s own dairy-free recipe rather than a copycat Disney Dole Whip recipe page, and the user only requested Dole Whip-style dessert rather than a Disney-copycat source.

R3.reason: No Sally’s Baking Addiction chocolate buttercream page is open and the response provides neither its six-ingredient list nor its 20-minutes-or-less total time; the user only asked generally for a chocolate option.

R4.reason: The open Inventables page is a general Easel software overview and the other X-Carve page concerns a drag chain, not a custom X-Carve photo-frame method, while the user requested a menu sign rather than a photo frame.

R5.reason: Apple’s AirPlay/screen-mirroring instructions are open in tab 9, and the response gives actionable Control Center steps plus same-Wi-Fi and Apple TV/AirPlay-TV/Mac destination requirements.

R6.reason: Apple’s iPad onscreen-keyboard guide is open in tab 5, and the response correctly says to pinch outward/open on the floating keyboard to restore full size.

R7.reason: The response provides an integrated concise plan and names the IGN and Dole tabs, but it does not leave open or identify a chocolate recipe comparison page such as the required Sally’s buttercream page.

P1_asked_for.reason: It supplied a complete BOTW reference, a Dole Whip-style tropical direction, a pineapple-free chocolate option, X-Carve guidance, iPhone mirroring, iPad keyboard restoration, and a final plan, though the chocolate option was an unsourced pudding concept rather than a kept-open recipe page.

P2_readable_for_them.reason: The clear headings, short steps, and concise final checklist suit a mobile, deadline-driven user, although the large tab dump and extra detail are more than this brief-leaning person likely needed.

P3_actionable.reason: The Dole recipe, AirPlay steps, keyboard gesture, and cautious CNC workflow are directly usable, but the chocolate dessert has no linked recipe or quantities and the X-Carve source is an overview rather than a verified start-to-carve tutorial.

P4_gap_handling.reason: It sensibly handled unspecified practical details by offering compatible AirPlay receiving-device options and recommending a simple shallow test carve on scrap, although it did not establish what receiving device or X-Carve materials the person actually has.

P5_overall.reason: This person would likely feel well served by the practical Zelda-themed concept and useful official links, with minor frustration from the non-recipe chocolate backup and the clutter of failed or irrelevant tabs left open.

missed_gaps: What device is available to receive the mirrored iPhone screen (Apple TV, AirPlay-compatible TV, or Mac).
What X-Carve model, bit, material, and prior machine setup the person has available for the sign.

P1_asked_for.reason: It supplied a comprehensive BOTW cookbook, a game-fitting Dole Whip-style tropical centerpiece, a pineapple-free chocolate concept, X-Carve guidance, Apple mirroring/keyboard steps, and a closing plan, though the chocolate option was not backed by a concrete recipe page.

P2_readable_for_them.reason: The headings, bullets, and direct steps are clear, but the answer and especially the full tab inventory are longer than ideal for a time-pressed, mobile, brief-preferring person.

P3_actionable.reason: The linked Dole and IGN pages, ingredient list, serving direction, CNC workflow, and Apple steps are usable immediately, but the chocolate pudding option lacks a specific recipe, quantities, or reliable recipe link.

P4_gap_handling.reason: It sensibly handled unprovided details by recommending a simple sign, scrap test, common AirPlay receivers, and a separate topping station, while stating the relevant conditions rather than pretending to know the user's equipment.

P5_overall.reason: This person would likely have a practical, cohesive dessert-table plan and usable references, with the main shortcomings being excess length and the less-developed chocolate backup.
